subject: Change in behavior of -R flag for featureCounts in version 1.5.0

messages.author: f24b6672b86b41b4
messages.subject: Change in behavior of -R flag for featureCounts in version 1.5.0
parts:
Hi,

I like to use the -R flag for featureCounts to report the assignment results per read. In version 1.4.4, it saved these results based on the input file name. For example, it saved the results in DIRNAME/FILENAME.featureCounts. I recently updated to version 1.5.0. Now instead of saving this output file in the same directory as the input file, it concatenates the directory and filename to save the file in the current working directory, e.g. DIRNAME.FILENAME.featureCounts. This is very inconvenient. The output of the program should not change based on the directory where I happen to run it.

Is it possible to return the -R flag to its previous behavior? Even better would be to allow the user to specify a filename to save these results. Personally I'd prefer to this file saved to the same place as the output file, not the input file. Allowing -R to accept a filename would allow each individual end user to save these results wherever they like.

Thanks,

John

messages.author: 6569f7247d312021
messages.subject: Re: Change in behavior of -R flag for featureCounts in version 1.5.0
parts:
Hi John,

Thanks for the suggestion. We will save the .featureCounts files generated from using -R flag to the same directory as the output count file. We will try to include this change in a January release.

Best wishes,
Wei

messages.subject: Re: Change in behavior of -R flag for featureCounts in version 1.5.0
parts:

Thank you for reverting this back to the original behavior. I confirmed that subread-1.5.0-p2 writes the .featureCounts file to the output directory.

John

messages.author: f24b6672b86b41b4
messages.subject: Re: Change in behavior of -R flag for featureCounts in version 1.5.0
parts:
Hi Wei,

Another quick follow up. I had a mistake in my last email. The original behavior was to save the the summary file as <input_file>.featureCounts. The new behavior, which is what I had requested, is to save the summary file as <output_file>.featureCounts. I make the distinction because the new behavior is working correctly, but the featureCounts standard error output still documents the old behavior. Using subread-1.5.0-p2-Linux-x86_64, the output has the following line:

||      Assignment details : <input_file>.featureCounts                       ||

Thanks,

John

messages.author: 6569f7247d312021
messages.subject: Re: Change in behavior of -R flag for featureCounts in version 1.5.0
parts:
Hi John,

The output from '-R' flag has always been saved to '<input_file>.featureCounts' files because we generate '.featureCounts' file for each input file.

The summary file, which includes the summary stats of read counting, is always saved to '<output_file>.summary'.

Wei

messages.author: f24b6672b86b41b4
messages.subject: Re: Change in behavior of -R flag for featureCounts in version 1.5.0
parts:
Hi Wei,

The .featureCounts file created with the -R flag does use the basename of each input BAM file, but they are not saved to the same direcotry as the input files. Consider the following hypothetical featureCounts call:

$ featureCounts -a exons.saf -F SAF -R -o outdir1/outdir2/results.txt indir1/indir2/file1.bam indir1/indir2/file2.bam

The -R flag creates two output files:

outdir1/outdir2/file1.bam.featureCounts
outdir1/outdir2/file2.bam.featureCounts

The description '<input_file>.featureCounts' in the log implies they will be saved to indir1/indir2. I think it would be more informative to output in the log "outdir1/outdir1/<input_file>.featureCounts".

Thanks,

John
